prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of policy proposals (2005 manifesto)

Funding and tax
- Reallocate about £5bn/year from lower-priority spending (end ID cards; abolish a central industry department and subsidies; redirect the Child Trust Fund to education).
- Introduce a 50% income tax rate on earnings above £100,000 to fund: scrapping university tuition/top-up fees; free personal care for elderly and disabled people; and lower local taxation.
- Replace Council Tax with a Local Income Tax, cutting the typical household bill by about £450; eight in ten pensioners would pay less.
- Independent scrutiny of budget figures by the National Audit Office; greater ONS independence.
- Raise stamp duty threshold to £150,000.

Health and care
- Free personal care for elderly and disabled people.
- Faster diagnosis via more scans/tests in community settings, evening/weekend use of scanners, and published test wait times.
- End charges for eye and dental check-ups; widen prescription charge exemptions after review.
- Recruit additional doctors, nurses and allied staff; reduce central targets; increase local accountability.
- Reform NHS dentistry; personalised care plans; stronger palliative and mental health rights.
- Public health: ban smoking in enclosed public places; nutrition standards for school meals; limits on unhealthy-food ads during children’s TV.

Education and skills
- Abolish tuition and top-up fees; restore maintenance grants for lower-income students.
- Use Child Trust Fund resources to hire 21,000 teachers; cut infant classes to avg. 20 and junior to 25; extend 8am–6pm provision; complete 3,500 Children’s Centres by 2010.
- Guarantee specialist teachers in core subjects; reduce high-stakes testing at ages 7 and 11; strengthen special educational needs support.
- Create a unified diploma framework blending academic and vocational routes; close funding gaps between schools and colleges.

Crime, justice, borders
- Cancel ID cards; fund 10,000 extra police and complete 20,000 community support officers; cut police bureaucracy and improve tech.
- Prioritise serious drug crime; expand tough community sentences for non-violent offenders; link prison education/training to release.
- Create a UK Border Force; maintain jury trial protections; enable use of intercept evidence; replace control orders with judge-led, time-limited measures if needed.
- Dedicated asylum agency; allow asylum seekers to work.
- Single Equality Act; hate-crime units in each force.

Economy and business
- Simpler, sunset-tested regulation; single inspectorate visits.
- Small business rate relief up to £1,500; shift to site-value rating.
- Create a duty to trade fairly; establish an English Tourism Board.
- Consult on euro entry via referendum when conditions are right; managed economic migration to meet skills needs.

Pensions, benefits, families
- From age 75: raise state pension to at least £109.45 (single) and £167.05 (couple), linked to earnings; introduce a residency-based citizen’s pension at 75.
- Maternity pay for first child: minimum wage level (£170/week) for six months.
- Replace the Child Support Agency with Inland Revenue assessment/enforcement and a specialist tribunal.
- £200 Winter Fuel Payment extended to severely disabled working-age people; option to take fuel payments as insulation vouchers.
- Strengthen compensation for workers who lost company pensions; honour accrued public-sector pension rights; simplify benefits and reduce fraud/error.

Housing, local services, culture
- Release public land for 100,000 affordable homes; VAT reforms to favour brownfield reuse; planning consent required for new second homes in pressured areas.
- Free councils from excessive central controls; merge inspectorates; protect post offices; maintain universal postal pricing.
- Restore lottery independence; end real-terms freeze on core arts funding; reduce VAT on historic repairs; increase grassroots sports funding; support the 2012 Olympic and Paralympic bid.

Transport
- Fewer, longer rail franchises tied to investment and performance; reinstate postponed rail upgrades; improve station safety.
- Reform Vehicle Excise Duty: zero for least-polluting vehicles and higher for the most polluting; expand congestion charging where congestion is severe with upfront public transport investment.
- Long term: replace fuel duty and VED with nationwide road pricing based on location, congestion and emissions.
- Free off-peak local bus travel for all pensioners and disabled people; free national rail discount cards for pensioners, disabled people, families and young people.
- Limit major new road-building; expand rail freight, ports and waterways.
- Aviation: per-aircraft charging; pursue inclusion in emissions trading; oppose new sites and South East expansions; protect lifeline routes.

Environment and energy
- Make at least 20% of electricity from renewables by 2020; do not replace ageing nuclear stations; strengthen incentives for energy efficiency and smaller, cleaner vehicles; convert the Climate Change Levy to a carbon tax.
- Waste: 60% household recycling within seven years; regular kerbside services; producer responsibility; restrict new incinerators to best-environment-option cases.
- Planning and building regulations aligned with carbon targets; greener public procurement; Environmental Responsibility Act; unify key environmental functions in one department.
- International: meet 0.5% of GNI aid by 2007/08 and 0.7% by 2011; end agricultural export dumping; promote sustainable development, biodiversity protection, and action against illegal logging/wildlife trade; lead on climate targets (long-term contraction and convergence).
- Rural: fair-trading duty with a Food Trade Inspector; CAP reform to support family farms and environmental stewardship; Marine Act with conservation zones; Animal Protection Commission and comprehensive Animal Welfare Act; no commercial GM until proven environmentally safe; GM-free zones and clear labelling.

Europe, defence, foreign policy
- Support EU institutional reforms via referendum; strengthen UN/EU effectiveness.
- Defence: address overstretch; improve procurement; reallocate from lower-priority programmes to frontline welfare; share burdens via NATO/EU; retain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral reductions; tighter arms export oversight and broker regulation; promote an international arms trade treaty.
- Iraq: support transition to legitimate government, strengthen local security forces and essential services, and aim to withdraw troops with the expiry of the UN mandate.

Constitutional and media reform
- War Powers Act requiring parliamentary approval for military action; Civil Service Act; stronger select committees; reduce and decentralise central government; devolve powers to local authorities and regions; fair funding across UK nations/regions.
- Electoral reform: Single Transferable Vote for local, devolved and Westminster elections; votes at the same age as for marriage/school-leaving/work; predominantly elected second chamber; more personalised EU elections.
- Replace the BBC’s governors with an independent regulator appointed by Parliament.
